I will still do wheat and maize on the same 16.9 mu, same as last year. For me, the first thing is not to make big changes. I have farmed this land a long time, and if I change too much, I may lose yield. Wheat needs a steady stand before winter, enough base fertilizer, and at least a few good irrigations because I have well water. Maize comes right after wheat, so I will not waste time. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because these are what many people around here use now, and if the seed is weak, the harvest suffers first. On fertilizer, I will not cut too hard. Fertilizer costs money, but losing grain costs more. For wheat I will put a bit more nitrogen, with phosphorus under the seed and some potassium too, then topdress nitrogen when the seedlings and crop need strength. For maize I will also feed it enough nitrogen, because if maize turns pale in summer, yield drops fast. Since my land has well irrigation, I will use water at the key times instead of gambling on rain. On pests, I will not spray too many times, but I will not wait until damage is heavy either. For tillage, I will keep it simple and practical: wheat after a proper plough or rotary preparation, maize after wheat with rotary tillage so I can sow on time. With 16.9 mu, I still have to watch every yuan, but this area is big enough that missing the right window hurts more than spending a little extra on seed, fertilizer, or one more irrigation.
